HTTP.overview: Application-level protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypermedia information systems based on a request-response model.
advantages: Ubiquitous support across all platforms
Human-readable plain text headers (in HTTP/1.1)
disadvantages: Head-of-line blocking in HTTP/1.1
High overhead per request due to uncompressed headers

HTTP/2.overview: Major revision of the HTTP network protocol derived from SPDY, focusing on reduced latency via multiplexing.
advantages: Multiplexing eliminates application-level head-of-line blocking
HPACK header compression reduces overhead
disadvantages: TCP-level head-of-line blocking remains
More complex implementation than HTTP/1.1

HTTP/3.overview: The third major version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, using QUIC instead of TCP to eliminate all head-of-line blocking.
advantages: No TCP head-of-line blocking
Faster connection establishment with 0-RTT handshakes
disadvantages: High CPU overhead for UDP packet processing
Blocked by some restrictive corporate firewalls

REST.overview: An architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems emphasizing stateless, cacheable interactions using standard HTTP methods.
advantages: High scalability due to statelessness
Leverages existing HTTP caching mechanisms
disadvantages: Over-fetching or under-fetching of data
Lack of strict typing compared to RPC frameworks

GraphQL.overview: A query language for APIs and a runtime for fulfilling those queries with existing data, allowing clients to request exactly what they need.
advantages: Eliminates over-fetching and under-fetching
Strongly typed schema provides automatic introspection
disadvantages: Complex server-side caching compared to REST
Risk of deeply nested queries causing performance bottlenecks

gRPC.overview: A high-performance, open-source universal RPC framework developed by Google utilizing Protocol Buffers and HTTP/2.
advantages: Highly efficient binary serialization
Native support for bi-directional streaming
disadvantages: Not natively supported in web browsers without proxies
Steeper learning curve than REST

tRPC.overview: End-to-end typesafe APIs made easy, designed specifically for TypeScript monorepos to share types without a build step.
advantages: Zero build steps or code generation needed
Incredible developer experience with instant type feedback
disadvantages: Only useful in TypeScript-to-TypeScript environments
Tightly couples client and server architectures

SOAP.overview: A protocol specification for exchanging structured information in the implementation of web services, heavily reliant on XML.
advantages: Built-in WS-Security provides enterprise-grade protection
ACID compliance and distributed transactions via WS-AtomicTransaction
disadvantages: Very verbose XML payloads lead to high bandwidth usage
Complex specification requires robust tooling

XML-RPC.overview: A remote procedure call protocol which uses XML to encode its calls and HTTP as a transport mechanism.
advantages: Simple human-readable XML format
Language agnostic with basic types
disadvantages: Lacks advanced security features
Verbose compared to modern JSON equivalents

JSON-RPC.overview: A stateless, light-weight remote procedure call protocol encoded in JSON.
advantages: Extremely lightweight and simple to implement
Supports batching multiple calls in one request
disadvantages: No native type schema definition
Lacks standard hypermedia links

Thrift.overview: A software framework for scalable cross-language services development originally developed at Facebook.
advantages: Provides both serialization and RPC stack
Supports multiple transport and protocol formats (binary, compact, JSON)
disadvantages: Less active community compared to gRPC
Documentation can be sparse

OData.overview: An open protocol to allow the creation and consumption of queryable and interoperable RESTful APIs.
advantages: Standardized syntax for filtering, sorting, and pagination
Rich metadata describes the data model
disadvantages: Very complex to implement fully from scratch
Payloads can include heavy metadata overhead

Avro.overview: A remote procedure call and data serialization framework developed within Apache's Hadoop project utilizing JSON for schemas and binary for data.
useCases: Schema evolution in big data pipelines
advantages: Schema is stored with the data for self-describing files
Excellent schema evolution capabilities
disadvantages: JSON schema definition can be verbose
Not widely used outside the Java/Big Data ecosystem for RPC

OpenAPI.overview: A specification for machine-readable interface files for describing, producing, consuming, and visualizing RESTful web services.
advantages: Massive ecosystem of tooling (Swagger UI, code generators)
Standardizes REST API definitions across teams
disadvantages: Keeping specs in sync with code requires effort or specific frameworks
Can become unwieldy for massive APIs

JSON:API.overview: A specification for how a client should request that resources be fetched or modified, and how a server should respond to those requests.
advantages: Highly standardized payload format prevents bikeshedding
Built-in support for sideloading related resources
disadvantages: Verbose JSON structure with mandatory nesting
Steep learning curve for developers used to simple REST

gRPC-Web.overview: A JavaScript client library that allows browser applications to access a gRPC service via a special proxy.
advantages: Brings gRPC typing and performance to the browser
Shares identical proto definitions with backend
disadvantages: Requires a proxy (like Envoy) to translate to standard gRPC
Lacks client and bidirectional streaming

Connect RPC.overview: A family of libraries for building browser and gRPC-compatible HTTP APIs using Protocol Buffers.
advantages: Works directly in the browser without Envoy proxy
Supports gRPC, gRPC-Web, and Connect protocols simultaneously
disadvantages: Newer ecosystem with fewer language integrations than standard gRPC
Still requires Protobuf tooling

OAuth 2.0.overview: An industry-standard protocol for authorization that enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service.
useCases: Social login integrations (Sign in with Google)
advantages: Separates authorization from authentication
Rich ecosystem with standardized grant types for different flows
disadvantages: Complexity in implementing securely (e.g., PKCE requirement)
Does not provide authentication (identity) natively

OIDC.overview: OpenID Connect is a simple identity layer on top of the OAuth 2.0 protocol, allowing clients to verify the identity of the end-user.
advantages: Provides standardized ID Tokens (JWT) for user information
Built on top of robust OAuth 2.0 flows
disadvantages: Token management and validation can be complex
Requires synchronized clocks for token expiration checks

WebAuthn.overview: A web standard published by the W3C that defines an API for creating and using strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials.
advantages: Phishing-resistant due to origin binding
No shared secrets stored on the server
disadvantages: Complex server-side implementation and attestation parsing
Account recovery flows when devices are lost can be tricky

SOAP 1.2.overview: An updated version of the SOAP protocol that provides improved interoperability and a clear processing model.
advantages: Standardized fault handling
Transport independent by design
disadvantages: Considered outdated for modern web dev
Heavy XML parsing overhead

SAML.overview: Security Assertion Markup Language is an XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between parties.
advantages: Mature, deeply embedded in enterprise infrastructure
Passes rich attribute assertions along with authentication
disadvantages: XML-based configuration is error-prone and complex
Generally not suited for native mobile apps or SPAs directly

CAS.overview: Central Authentication Service is a single sign-on protocol for the web, heavily used in academia.
advantages: Simple proxy authentication flow
Open-source reference implementation is highly extensible
disadvantages: Less industry adoption outside higher education than SAML/OIDC
Requires central CAS server infrastructure

Kafka.overview: A distributed event streaming platform using a custom binary TCP-based protocol for high-throughput, low-latency event processing.
advantages: Massively scalable and highly available
Persistent storage allows rewinding and replaying events
disadvantages: Zookeeper/KRaft operational complexity
Not natively meant for traditional RPC or targeted message routing

RabbitMQ.overview: A widely used open-source message broker that natively implements the AMQP protocol.
advantages: Extremely flexible routing via exchanges and bindings
Supports multiple protocols (AMQP, MQTT, STOMP)
disadvantages: Can suffer performance degradation under massive queue backlogs
Clustering can be fragile in network partition scenarios

AMQP.overview: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol is an open standard application layer protocol for message-oriented middleware.
advantages: Standardized wire-level protocol ensures interoperability across languages
Robust reliability guarantees (at-least-once, exactly-once semantics)
disadvantages: Protocol specification is heavily complex
High overhead per connection compared to lightweight protocols

MQTT.overview: A lightweight, publish-subscribe network protocol that transports messages between devices, designed for constrained devices and low-bandwidth.
advantages: Extremely small packet headers (2 bytes minimum)
Built-in Quality of Service (QoS 0, 1, 2) levels
disadvantages: No native message persistence queries for offline clients (outside of Retain flag)
Centralized broker can become a bottleneck

MQTT 5.overview: The latest major revision of the MQTT protocol, adding features like user properties, shared subscriptions, and improved error reporting.
advantages: Shared subscriptions allow load balancing across subscribers
Message properties allow custom metadata without altering payloads
disadvantages: Broker and client library support is still catching up compared to MQTT 3.1.1
Increased specification complexity

SQS.overview: Amazon Simple Queue Service is a fully managed message queuing service via HTTP API that enables decoupling of microservices.
advantages: Virtually unlimited throughput and scalability out of the box
Zero operational overhead or infrastructure management
disadvantages: Strictly pull-based, requires long-polling from clients
Message ordering only guaranteed in specialized FIFO queues with lower throughput limits

Webhook.overview: A method of augmenting or altering the behavior of a web page or web application with custom callbacks via HTTP POST.
advantages: Simple to consume using standard web frameworks
Real-time updates without polling overhead
disadvantages: Requires the consumer to have a publicly accessible endpoint
At-least-once delivery requires consumer idempotency

STOMP.overview: Simple (or Streaming) Text Oriented Messaging Protocol provides an interoperable wire format so that clients can talk to any message broker.
useCases: Web browsers communicating with message brokers (Spring Boot WebSockets)
advantages: Text-based protocol is very easy to debug and implement
Natively supported over WebSockets by many brokers
disadvantages: Higher overhead due to string encoding compared to binary protocols
Lacks advanced messaging features of AMQP

XMPP.overview: Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol is an open XML-based protocol for near-real-time messaging, presence, and contact list maintenance.
advantages: Decentralized and federated architecture
Highly extensible via XEPs (XMPP Extension Protocols)
disadvantages: XML parsing is resource-intensive on mobile
Presence storms can consume massive bandwidth

JMS.overview: Java Message Service is a Java API that allows applications to create, send, receive, and read messages.
advantages: Abstracts away the underlying message broker implementation
Strong transactional support
disadvantages: Tightly coupled to the Java ecosystem
Not a wire protocol, just an API standard

NATS.overview: A simple, high-performance open source messaging system for cloud native applications, IoT messaging, and microservices architectures.
advantages: Extremely lightweight with ultra-low latency
Zero-allocation server design provides massive throughput
disadvantages: Core NATS is 'at-most-once' delivery (requires JetStream for persistence)
Smaller ecosystem compared to Kafka

WebPush.overview: A protocol built on HTTP/2 that enables application servers to send push messages to web browsers.
advantages: Works even when the web app is closed via Service Workers
Standardized across major browsers
disadvantages: Requires user permission which is often denied
Payload sizes are restricted by browser push services

ZeroMQ.overview: A high-performance asynchronous messaging library, aimed at use in distributed or concurrent applications.
advantages: Brokerless architecture avoids single points of failure
Blistering fast throughput due to running in-memory or raw sockets
disadvantages: No built-in persistent message queuing
Complex low-level socket management falls on the developer

Pulsar.overview: Apache Pulsar is a cloud-native, distributed messaging and streaming platform originally created at Yahoo.
advantages: Separation of compute (brokers) and storage (BookKeeper) enables easy scaling
Native multi-tenancy support
disadvantages: High operational complexity with multiple moving parts (Zookeeper, BookKeeper, Brokers)
Steeper learning curve than Kafka

Celery.overview: An asynchronous task queue/job queue based on distributed message passing, primarily used in the Python ecosystem.
advantages: Seamless integration with Python web frameworks
Supports complex workflows (chains, chords)
disadvantages: Python-centric, difficult to use polyglot workers
Can silently fail if broker limits are reached without strict monitoring

SNS.overview: Amazon Simple Notification Service is a managed service that provides message delivery from publishers to subscribers.
advantages: Fully managed with extremely high durability
Supports multiple diverse endpoints (HTTP, SQS, Email)
disadvantages: Payloads are limited in size (256KB)
Debugging failed deliveries can be opaque without CloudWatch

ActiveMQ.overview: An open source, multi-protocol, Java-based message broker written by Apache.
advantages: Supports a vast array of protocols simultaneously
Rich enterprise features like message groups and exclusive consumers
disadvantages: Higher memory footprint compared to modern brokers like NATS
Can be complex to configure for high availability (KahaDB/Zookeeper)

RocketMQ.overview: A distributed messaging and streaming platform with low latency, high performance and reliability, created by Alibaba.
advantages: Native support for distributed transactional messages
Extremely stable under massive traffic spikes
disadvantages: Less documentation in English compared to Kafka
Smaller ecosystem outside of China/Java applications

IronMQ.overview: A managed message queue service designed for high availability and robust cloud application architectures.
advantages: Easy to use REST API interface
Push queues natively support webhook endpoints
disadvantages: Less ubiquitous than AWS SQS
Pricing can scale quickly with volume

Kinesis.overview: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is a serverless streaming data service that makes it easy to capture, process, and store data streams.
advantages: Deeply integrated with AWS ecosystem (Lambda, Redshift)
Managed sharding and scaling (in On-Demand mode)
disadvantages: Strict throughput limits per shard require careful capacity planning
Read amplification issues when multiple consumers read one stream

EventBridge.overview: A serverless event bus that makes it easier to build event-driven applications at scale using events generated from your applications or AWS services.
advantages: Advanced content-based event routing and filtering
Schema registry handles automatic schema discovery
disadvantages: Latency is higher than dedicated brokers like Kafka
Complex routing rules can become hard to manage

WebSocket.overview: A computer communications protocol, providing full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection.
advantages: Eliminates HTTP polling overhead for real-time data
Full-duplex allows server to push to client instantly
disadvantages: Stateful connections make load balancing and scaling difficult
Does not natively support multiplexing (unlike HTTP/2)

WebRTC.overview: A free, open-source project providing web browsers and mobile applications with real-time communication via simple APIs.
advantages: Ultra-low latency due to direct P2P connections
Built-in NAT traversal (STUN/TURN) and encryption
disadvantages: Highly complex signaling server setup required
Performance degrades in huge multi-party meshes (requires SFU/MCU)

SSE (Server-Sent Events).overview: A standard describing how servers can initiate data transmission towards clients once an initial client connection has been established.
advantages: Extremely simple to implement over standard HTTP
Built-in reconnection and event ID tracking in browsers
disadvantages: Unidirectional (Server to Client only)
Strictly limited to text/UTF-8 data (no binary)

TCP.overview: Transmission Control Protocol is a core protocol of the Internet Protocol Suite providing reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery.
advantages: Guarantees in-order delivery without data loss
Built-in congestion control prevents network collapse
disadvantages: High latency overhead from 3-way handshake
Head-of-line blocking affects real-time streams

UDP.overview: User Datagram Protocol provides a connectionless datagram service that prioritizes time over reliability.
advantages: Minimal overhead with no handshake
No head-of-line blocking allows immediate processing
disadvantages: No guarantee of delivery or ordering
Requires application layer to handle packet loss and congestion

RTMP.overview: Real-Time Messaging Protocol was initially a proprietary protocol for streaming audio, video and data over the Internet to Flash players.
advantages: Very low latency (1-3 seconds) for live streaming
Widely supported by streaming hardware and software encoders (OBS)
disadvantages: Flash is dead, making client-side playback unsupported in modern browsers
Vulnerable to firewall blocking on port 1935

HLS.overview: HTTP Live Streaming is an HTTP-based adaptive bitrate streaming communications protocol developed by Apple.
useCases: VOD (Video on Demand) platforms like Netflix
advantages: Works seamlessly through standard firewalls and CDNs
Adaptive bitrate ensures smooth playback on varying network speeds
disadvantages: High latency (traditionally 10-30 seconds) compared to RTMP/WebRTC
Apple-centric origins required fragmented implementations early on

MPEG-DASH.overview: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP is an international standard for adaptive bitrate streaming.
advantages: Codec agnostic, unlike older versions of HLS
True international ISO standard preventing vendor lock-in
disadvantages: Not natively supported by Apple Safari/iOS without MSE wrappers
Manifest files (MPD) are complex XML structures

WebTransport.overview: A web API that uses HTTP/3 protocol for bi-directional transport, designed for sending data between clients and servers reliably and unreliably.
advantages: Supports both reliable streams and unreliable datagrams in one API
Shares HTTP/3 port, avoiding firewall issues of raw UDP
disadvantages: Relatively new, lacking deep legacy browser support
Requires HTTP/3 infrastructure which is complex to deploy

QUIC.overview: A general-purpose transport layer network protocol designed by Google that reduces latency compared to TCP.
advantages: Connection migration survives IP address changes (e.g., WiFi to Cellular)
Zero RTT connection establishment on returning requests
disadvantages: High CPU utilization for packet decryption in userspace
Throttled by some enterprise UDP rate limiters

Socket.IO.overview: A library that enables real-time, bidirectional and event-based communication between the browser and the server.
advantages: Automatic fallback to HTTP long-polling if WebSockets are blocked
Built-in support for broadcasting and rooms/namespaces
disadvantages: Custom protocol wire format means clients MUST use Socket.IO libraries
Heavier overhead than raw WebSockets

SignalR.overview: A software library for Microsoft ASP.NET that allows server code to send asynchronous notifications to client-side web applications.
advantages: Deep integration with .NET Core ecosystem and authentication
Automatically manages connection negotiation and fallbacks
disadvantages: Ties backend architecture tightly to Microsoft/C# ecosystem
Requires sticky sessions if scaling out without a backplane (Redis)

WebSockets (WSS).overview: The secure version of the WebSocket protocol, encrypting all communication over TLS to prevent eavesdropping.
advantages: Provides privacy and data integrity via TLS
Bypasses transparent proxies that might disrupt plain WS
disadvantages: TLS handshake adds slight initial latency overhead
Certificate management required on servers

RTSP.overview: Real Time Streaming Protocol is a network control protocol designed for use in entertainment and communications systems to control streaming media servers.
advantages: Provides VCR-like controls (play, pause, record) remotely
Decouples control channel from the actual media delivery (RTP)
disadvantages: Not natively supported by web browsers
Often struggles with NAT traversal without specialized gateways

SRT.overview: Secure Reliable Transport is an open source video transport protocol that enables the delivery of high-quality and secure, low-latency video across the public Internet.
advantages: Built-in packet loss recovery utilizing ARQ
Pristine video quality over unpredictable networks (like public internet)
disadvantages: Still gaining adoption in consumer end-devices compared to HLS
Can introduce slight latency for packet retransmission buffers
